title: A session on a work/<id> branch that is not that item's worker opens a work window no land closes
goal: Found in the SP-mlemdqbn review (TK-nwxefymo): ql_capture.branch_row writes a branch row for any session whose hook cwd is on a work/<id> branch, so a main checkout left on a stale work/<id> branch (no item file), an orchestrator whose hook cwd passed through a worker worktree (cwd follows cd: kb/public/claude/hooks.md), or a session in a worktree after the item was done opens a window that only a shell backlog.py done or release of that session closes; land runs done as its own subprocess, so the orchestrator's later prompts count on the item or, with no item file, move from the sprint line to shared. branch_row writes only when the item file exists with status doing and the session's rows hold no claim, done or release of that item; usage.md and querylog.md say so. Unverified lead: a one-prompt claude -p worker gets its usage row only from the SessionEnd distill.

run:
import json,os,subprocess as sp,sys,tempfile,shutil
from pathlib import Path
S=Path.cwd();t=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp());c=1
try:
    g=lambda *a:sp.run(['git','-c','user.name=t','-c','user.email=t@t',*a],cwd=t/'r',capture_output=True,check=True)
    (t/'r').mkdir();g('init','-q');(t/'r'/'f').write_text('x');g('add','f');g('commit','-qm','i');g('checkout','-qb','work/ST-zzzzzzzz')
    os.environ['CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA']=str(t/'d');os.environ['CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT']=str(S);(t/'d'/'querylog').mkdir(parents=True);(t/'d'/'querylog'/'config.json').write_text('{"mode": "local"}')
    sys.path.insert(0,str(S/'_tools'));import ql_capture as q
    sp_=q.spool_dir();assert sp_ is not None and str(sp_).startswith(str(t)),'spool not in the temp dir'
    sp_.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    r=q.branch_row(sp_,'s1',{'cwd':str(t/'r')},'p1')
    print('branch row for a work/<id> branch with no item file:',r and r.get('item'));c=0 if r is None else 1
except Exception as x:print('check error',type(x).__name__,str(x)[:150])
finally:shutil.rmtree(t,ignore_errors=True)
sys.exit(c)
